BALANCE OF PAYMENTS - The first quarterly current account deficit data since the scrapping of monthly data is expected to show a deficit of A$4.5 to A$5.0 billion -- or roughly A$1.5 to A$1.7 billion a month. This is a improvement on the December

quarter and economists said given that the monthly trade balance showed a A$137 million surplus over the first quarter, it will help reinforce the underlying net debt problem Australia faces. After being a detraction in the December quarter, net exports are expected to make a small positive contribution to GDP.

RETAIL TRADE/MOTOR REGISTRATIONS - The data will give an idea of how retail spending has held up into the second quarter, and will be especially interesting in light of the RBA's rate cut on Friday. Retail spending began the year very strongly, but has since showed some signs of softening. The fact the Easter

period fell totally in March may also be a risk that the April data may be weak, economists said. After three strong monthly rises, economists expect registrations to be flat but said the trend would still be quite strongly positive.
